page: Microsoft Azure E32a_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the EAv4 series, virtualized under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system is provisioned with 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 7763 processor running at an indicated clock speed of 3.525 GHz. Its x86_64 architecture incorporates 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache per core cluster. Instruction set extensions include standard AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI, but lack AVX-512 and AMX extensions. System memory is scaled to 256.0 GB of RAM, preserving an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, complemented by 859 GB of bundled local SSD storage. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs.

Benchmark outcomes show reliable multi-threaded compute and memory throughput. The instance recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 14,434.0, a PassMark CPU score of 32,467.2, and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 12,263.78, placing it consistently in the middle tier of tested hardware. Single-core performance sits lower, highlighted by a stress-ng single-core rating of 769.39 in the bottom percentile, though Geekbench single-core reached 1,599.0. Memory throughput delivered 112.96 GB/sec for uncached large reads and 57.02 GB/sec for uncached writes, enabling Redis to attain 31.85 million SET operations per second.

Hardware tradeoffs focus on dense memory capacity and concurrent throughput rather than peak per-core speed or vector-heavy mathematical workloads. In execution tasks like Geekbench image processing and small-scale LLM generation (292.29 tokens/sec on a 135M model), it exhibits strong efficiency. However, large model processing drops off significantly, down to 6.6 tokens/sec for 70B prompt processing. The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU allocation coupled with integrated local SSD storage positions this VM for enterprise in-memory databases, large data caches, relational databases, and multi-threaded analytical services.
description: Microsoft Azure E32a_v4 is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7763 processor clocked at 3.525 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under Hyper-V, it provides 256.0 GB of RAM—yielding an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio—along with 859 GB of local SSD storage and no GPUs. Standard AVX, AES, and SHA_NI vector and cryptographic extensions are supported, while AVX-512 is omitted. Benchmarks demonstrate stable mid-tier multi-core execution (14,434.0 Geekbench multi-core and 32,467.2 PassMark CPU), alongside a Redis rate of 31.85 million SET operations per second and 112.96 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. Single-core throughput is modest relative to its multi-threaded scale. With dense memory allocation and integrated SSD space, the server is balanced for in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise memory-bound data processing.
